display.purpose: Latin game lettering; no global size is implied.

body.purpose: General text in the self-hosted Fusion Pixel stack.

number.purpose: Quantities and keyboard hints at component-specific sizes.

motion.name: room-fire
motion.purpose: Local furnace-light opacity loop; disabled by OS preference and in-game setting.

motion.name: guide-beacon
motion.purpose: Current objective outline; disabled by OS preference and in-game setting.

motion.name: hammer-swing
motion.purpose: Slow lift, fast strike, contact hold and heavy recovery; immediate presentation under OS or in-game Reduce Motion.

motion.name: anvil-shake
motion.purpose: Contact-synchronized 6px local recoil with 160ms room shake; suppressed by OS or in-game Reduce Motion.

motion.name: result-pop
motion.purpose: Result banner after a real forging action.

motion.name: button-state
motion.value: transform .08s ease, filter .12s ease, border-color .12s ease

motion.name: in-game-reduce-motion
motion.purpose: Setting also suppresses ambient particles and shake, and reduces event particles to roughly 30%; OS preference alone only stops room/guide loops.

narrative.overview:
The workshop is a continuous, fixed-camera 2D pixel-art room. Soot-dark stone, timber, iron, brass, and living furnace light establish the world. Crisp Chinese pixel lettering and compact numerical readouts let the player act inside it.

The room carries the spatial story; controls and information sit near the objects they affect. The generated background and transparent anvil share the stage with procedural sword art, authored SVG props, and result particles. Short introduction copy establishes the blacksmith's predicament, then the first day's tutorial follows actual play. This document records the current implementation; it does not establish full equivalence with the original game.
keyCharacteristics: Continuous desktop room with a central foreground sword and anvil.
Charcoal and soot neutrals, ember heat, brass actions, and parchment text.
Crisp raster clusters, authored pixel geometry, and self-hosted pixel fonts.
Contextual instruction and outcome-driven forging feedback.

rules.name: The State Has a Name Rule
rules.body: Pair heat, risk, resource, and completion colors with labels or figures; color alone does not explain a game state.

rules.name: The Pixel Lettering Rule
rules.body: Use the supplied pixel families for the game's voice, and preserve the Chinese fallback stack. Do not replace them with a smooth display face.

rules.name: The Scene Carries the Room Rule
rules.body: Let floor, wall, light, and props continue between controls. Add backing only where text or interaction needs it.

dos: **Do** keep the accepted desktop composition as one continuous 2D pixel-art room.
**Do** use generated scenery and transparent props alongside the procedural game assets, with nearest-neighbor rendering.
**Do** keep live state, quantities, probabilities, controls, and instruction in readable UI layers.
**Do** preserve visible resource names, keyboard focus, drag/drop affordances, and the actual first-day outcome.
**Do** describe the in-game and OS reduced-motion behaviors accurately.
donts: **Don't** rebuild the workshop as three nonoverlapping webpage panels and a detached footer.
**Don't** bake labels or interactive state into scenery, or duplicate the foreground sword and anvil in the room plate.
**Don't** treat inherited mobile CSS as a newly approved product target.
**Don't** change game odds or claim complete original-game equivalence through visual documentation.
**Don't** canonize inherited eyebrow labels, hard offset shadows, decorative halos, or unverified contrast as rules for new surfaces.
